core.title: Keep every referenced train sequence equal to its interlocking route projection
core.given: An interlocking route references a train, so the route has a projected sequence and the train has its own sequence.
core.when: Any referenced train sequence is checked at the confirmation phase (CONFIRM) — whether or not you edited the route or the train in this plan (editing either side is the common way to introduce a mismatch).
core.then: Make the referenced train sequence equal the interlocking route projection step by step on step, intent, from, to and artifact.
prefer: Change the route and the referenced train sequence in the same plan step so they stay equal.
Compare step by step on all five fields (step, intent, from, to, artifact) for every referenced train before handing off to the confirmation phase, including untouched ones.
avoid: Matching only some fields (e.g. same steps but different artifact or from/to) and calling the sequences equivalent.
Editing only one side and leaving the other to drift.
Removing the train reference or editing the checker's expected projection only to get rid of the failure.
core.why: Guard coverage and the rest of the route reasoning are proven against the route-to-train projection, so a train that diverges from its route breaks that proof. The check is strict and blocks the confirmation phase.
evidence: The stack's projection-equivalence check passes for every interlocking route that references a train.
Any failure pinpoints the interlocking, route and train involved, the offending step and field, and the expected versus actual values; with zero such failures the rule is satisfied.
verification: A coherence check resolves each interlocking route's train reference and compares the referenced train sequence with the route projection step by step on step, intent, from, to and artifact (the projection-equivalence term).

Checked in the confirmation phase (CONFIRM) and confirm-blocking; disposition strict, severity 4 — any mismatch on the five fields fails, including pre-existing mismatches not touched by the current change.

The check covers every train an interlocking route references, edited or not; it does not cover trains that no route references, and differences outside the five fields (e.g. prose or metadata) do not fail.
Each failure reports the interlocking, route and train identifiers, the offending step and field, and the expected versus actual values.
An edit-triggered early warning (a diff observer resolving route-to-train references while either side is edited) is optional and not a prerequisite; absence of an edit does not exempt a sequence.

fires: The confirmation phase runs and any interlocking route references a train whose sequence differs from the route projection in step order, intent, from, to or artifact — including mismatches that already existed and were not touched in this change.
A planner edits an interlocking route so its projection now differs from the referenced train sequence.
A planner edits a train sequence that an interlocking route references, without updating the route projection.
A new interlocking route references an existing train whose sequence does not match the route projection.
doesNotFire: A train that no interlocking route references.

A referenced train whose sequence already equals the route projection on step, intent, from, to and artifact (e.g. only prose/metadata differs); any mismatch on those five fields still fires regardless of what was edited.

profileRequirements.meaning: Which concrete plan-artifact kinds are the interlocking spec (the subject) and the train specs its routes reference, so the check can recognize and resolve them in this stack.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention operates on plan-notation artifacts (interlocking routes, train sequences, the route projection and its five fields), which are stack-independent by construction, so the core carries the obligation unchanged. The only Bun-specific content is the validator identity — the validator test id in evidence[0] and the validation family/template/variant registry ids in verifier_detail[1] — classified bunOnly, with the core describing the check generically. CONFIRM, confirm-blocking, strict disposition and severity 4 are per-rule verification facts kept in core:verification, not profile keys. One profile requirement (roles.plan_artifact.kinds) suffices to instantiate the file-kind fact for another stack; nothing was missing from the vocabulary, so proposedKeys is empty. The exact failure-field names (interlocking_id, route_id, train_id, step, field, expected, actual) were kept in the core because they are domain-level, not stack-specific.
